newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu pledges to strengthen hold on West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu pledges to strengthen hold on West Bank.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pledged at the funeral on Thursday of a Jewish settler and her son who were killed by Arab guerrillas to sink Israeli roots deeper into the occupied West Bank.

"Our first answer to these murderers and animals is that the government and people of Israel will stay here, build here and live here," he said at the funeral attended by thousands at the settlement of Beit El.
"We will remember Etta and Ephraim (Tzur) with every house we build, every road we pave, every family we raise," Netanyahu, his voice cracking, said at their graveside.

As the woman and boy were laid to rest, a spokesman in Damascus for the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestinian said it carried out the shooting that also wounded her husband and four other children in the car.
"We confirm our responsibility for the attack which comes within the PFLP's policy of fighting settlers wherever they are," Maher al-Taher told Reuters.

Netanyahu's attendance, along with other senior cabinet members, at the burial of the mother of seven and her 12-year-old son was a show of solidarity and reconciliation with the more than 130,000-strong settler community in the West Bank.

Settlers have been highly critical of Netanyahu's negotiations with the PLO on implementing an Israeli troop redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron, where some 400 Jews live and study amidst 100,000 Palestinians.

The drive-by shooting at the Tzur family car on Wednesday near the self-ruled town of Ramallah drew settler calls for Netanyahu, who won election last May vowing to make Israel safer from guerrilla attack, to get tougher on security.
A settler leader urged the government to respond to the incident by settling more Jews in areas seized by Israel in the 1967 Middle East war.
"For any Jewish blood spilled, 1,000 Jewish families will come here to live," Pinhas Wallerstein, head of the Council of Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza, told Israel Radio.
Since taking office in June, the right-wing Netanyahu government has given the go-ahead for the construction of thousands of homes in existing settlements but has yet to establish any new outposts.

"I know you are worried about the future," Netanyahu said over a loudspeaker at the funeral as calls to prayer from a Moslem muezzin in a nearby Arab village echoed across the windswept terraced hills.
"I want to remove this fear from your hearts because we will increase the efforts and resources which we will invest here to ensure the existence of the Jewish people on its historic land."
Netanyahu heaped praise on the settlers, mainly religious Jews who believe they have a God-given right to settle in the biblical Land of Israel.
"The time has come to say after dozens of years of defamation and slander, from abroad and at home, against these people that there are none better than them.
"There are none more wonderful and none like them to carry on Israeli tradition and love of Israel -- and the Land of Israel -- which we all share," the prime minister said.
Israel said the guerrillas escaped into Ramallah, which it closed off after the attack.
At the funeral, Netanyahu demanded the Palestinian Authority hand them over for trial in Israel if they are captured.
In the past, the self-rule administration has tried Arabs suspected of carrying out attacks in Israel, saying interim peace deals allowed such judicial action in lieu of extradition.

Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, asked by reporters in Gaza to comment on the killings, kept silent. A PLO official said the Palestinian Authority, which runs self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza, condemned the attack.
Yoel Tzur had bitter words for Arafat as he laid his wife and son to rest. "He must know that for every Jew that is attacked, a Jewish settlement will grow."
